questions.q: What does the APG node do at its default eta of 1?
options: Keeps both parts of the guidance whole, so only the length limit can act
questions.answer: Keeps both parts of the guidance whole, so only the length limit can act
questions.why: eta multiplies the parallel part. At 1 orth + par is the original vector.

questions.q: Which of the four adds extra model predictions per step?
questions.why: All four work on predictions the sampler already has.

questions.q: What does RescaleCFG match the result's spread to?
questions.why: ro_pos over ro_cfg scales the cfg result, then the multiplier blends.

questions.q: CFGNorm strength 0.5 does what, in its default mode?
options: Blends halfway back to plain cfg
questions.why: The default branch returns pred * scale * strength.

questions.q: What is the likely reason CFG-Zero-Star barely changed our SDXL render?
options: If alpha stays near 1 the sum hardly moves, and it does not try to limit size
questions.answer: If alpha stays near 1 the sum hardly moves, and it does not try to limit size
questions.why: The stored difference is 2.17. We didn't log alpha on that run, but alpha near 1 leaves the sum almost alone. Zero-init isn't in the core node.

questions.q: With APG's limits off and node cfg s, the result equals
options: Plain cfg one higher than the node's setting
Plain cfg at exactly the node's setting
questions.answer: Plain cfg one higher than the node's setting
questions.why: Checked against the real node: modified_cond gives pos + s times guidance, which is plain cfg at s + 1.
